idiom_name: MikroORM EntitySchema + EntityManager (identity map + unit of work)
implementation_notes: TypeScript types vanish at runtime, so a mapper needs runtime metadata: MikroORM keeps it outside the class with EntitySchema (or inside with decorators) and implements the pattern properly - an EntityManager that is both identity map and unit of work, with persist/find then flush as the write step. TypeORM offers a repository-based DataMapper mode and Prisma generates a typed client instead of mapping your own classes, while Sequelize and Mongoose are Active Record implementations. Keep one EntityManager per request (em.fork()), because both the identity map and the change set are scoped to it.
pitfalls: The identity map belongs to the EntityManager: a global or reused EM leaks entities and stale reads between requests - fork one per request.
Class fields must be initialised or declared with !; because types are erased, a field missing from the schema exists only in the type system and silently never persists.
Lazy Reference/Collection values must be awaited inside the unit of work; touching an unloaded collection afterwards throws.
Decorator-based mapping needs experimentalDecorators, emitDecoratorMetadata and reflect-metadata; EntitySchema avoids both but you then maintain the metadata by hand.
